transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… well, I almost didn’t come in because I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is, but it scared me a little. I’ve been hearing my name being called, like from the hallway at home, and once at the warehouse too when nobody was there. It sounds really real, like my husband is standing right next to me saying it. I know that probably sounds strange… is that the kind of thing I should tell you?
Have you heard your name being called more than once?

Yes… more than once. It’s not like it’s happening constantly or anything, but I’ve heard my name called from the hallway at home, and then once at the warehouse when nobody was there. It sounded really real, like my husband was right next to me saying it. I wasn’t sure if that’s something I should be worried about, but it did scare me.
Do you hear anything else besides your name being called?

Not really… I mean, the main thing is just my name being called. That’s what scared me enough to come in. It’ll sound like it’s coming from the hallway at home, and that one time at the warehouse when nobody was there. It sounds so real, like my husband is standing right next to me. I’m not trying to be dramatic, but that’s the part that bothered me.
Is it always your name that you hear being called, or have you heard any other voices or sounds?

It’s… it’s really just my name, as far as I can tell. I haven’t heard, like, conversations or anything like that. It’s just my name being called, from the hallway at home, and that one time at the warehouse when nobody was there. It sounds very real, like my husband is right next to me saying it… that’s what scared me enough to come in.
Have you ever heard any other voices, even if they are not calling your name?

I don’t think so… not other voices exactly. It’s mostly just my name. That’s the part that scared me enough to come in, because I’ll hear it from the hallway at home, and once at the warehouse when nobody was there. It sounds really real, like my husband is standing right next to me saying it. Is that… is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you hear your name being called all the time or just sometimes?

Just sometimes. It’s not like it’s nonstop or anything. It’s happened at home, like from the hallway, and then once at the warehouse when nobody was there. But when it does happen, it sounds really real… like my husband is right next to me calling my name. That’s what scared me enough to come in.
Have you ever done something in response to hearing your name being called?

Not really anything big, no. I mean… I’ll usually stop and look, or I’ll go check the hallway because it sounds so real, like my husband is right there calling me. At work that one time, I looked around the warehouse, but nobody was there. That’s what scared me enough to come in, honestly.
Has hearing your name being called caused you any problems or distress in your daily life?

It’s… not ruining my whole day or anything, but yeah, it has upset me. I get kind of scared because it sounds so real, like my husband is right next to me calling my name, and then nobody’s there. At home I’ll hear it from the hallway, and that one time at the warehouse really bothered me because I was sure someone was there. That’s why I thought I should come in, just to make sure I’m handling it the right way.
Has hearing your name being called affected your ability to work or interact with others?

A little, yeah… I mean, I’m still going to work and trying to keep things normal, but I have made some inventory mistakes—enough that my supervisor pulled me aside. That was embarrassing.

At home, my husband’s been taking over more of the bills and the usual routines because I’m not really keeping up like I should. And socially… I’ve kind of stopped showing up for my church pantry shifts and book club, which isn’t really like me. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it has been affecting things.
Have you seen anything unusual that wasn't really there?

No… I don’t think I’ve seen anything, like visually, that wasn’t there. It’s more been the hearing my name thing — from the hallway at home, and that one time at the warehouse. It sounds so real, like my husband is standing right next to me calling me, but then nobody’s there. That’s the part that scared me enough to come in.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

Yeah… I guess I have been feeling pretty down. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but after all that running around and arguing, I kind of just… dropped. Like this heavy, empty feeling.

Sometimes I’ll just sit at the kitchen table and start crying over nothing, and then I feel silly about it because I can’t really explain why. It’s like I can’t get myself back to normal, if that makes sense.
Have you been enjoying things you usually like to do?

Not really, no… I mean, I keep telling myself I’ll get back to it, but I haven’t touched my knitting basket, and my garden beds are just sitting there. I haven’t gone to book club or signed up for the church food pantry either.

It’s not that I stopped caring exactly… it just all feels like too much trouble, and then I think, “What’s the point?” I don’t know if that’s the right way to say it.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, empty feeling?

I think… about three months, maybe. Not every single minute, so I don’t want to overstate it, but that heavy, withdrawn feeling has kind of been hanging over me that long.

It’s just gotten harder to manage these past few weeks, if that makes sense.
Have you lost interest in things that you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I guess I have. I don’t mean that I never care about anything, but I just haven’t been doing the things I normally like.

My knitting basket is just sitting there, and the garden beds too. I haven’t gone back to book club, and I didn’t sign up for the church food pantry like I usually would. It all just feels like too much trouble, I guess… like not worth starting. Is that what you mean?
Have you had thoughts of death or suicide?

Um… I don’t think I’d say I want to kill myself, exactly. I don’t want you to think I’m… you know, dangerous or anything.

But I have had thoughts like… maybe it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And that scares me to even say, because I don’t want to be that kind of person. I haven’t made any plan to hurt myself or anything like that. It’s more just… those thoughts come up sometimes.
Have you had difficulty sleeping or have you been sleeping more than usual?

Yeah… I mean, I am sleeping, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. But lately when I do fall asleep, I keep waking up over and over, usually before my alarm.

Then I get to work and I’m dragging myself through my stock list like I didn’t really rest at all. Does that count as trouble sleeping?
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

I don’t know if it’s been a significant amount, exactly… I haven’t really been keeping track of the scale.

My eating’s been kind of off, though. Some days I get caught up in planning things and I’ll realize I basically forgot to eat. Then other days, nothing sounds good and I just pick at toast or something. So… maybe my appetite’s changed, yes. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you felt hopeless about the future?

I… I don’t want to say hopeless like I’ve completely given up, because that sounds so bad. But yes, sometimes after all the running around and arguing, I just kind of… drop.

I’ll sit at the kitchen table and start crying over nothing, and it feels heavy and empty, like I can’t get myself back to normal. I don’t know if that’s what you mean by hopeless, but it feels close to that.
How long have you been feeling sad or down?

I guess… it’s been there for maybe about three months, that sad, pulled-back feeling. I was still managing, mostly, so I didn’t want to make a big thing of it.

But these last few weeks, it’s gotten harder to sort of push through. Does that answer it the right way?
Have you felt like you're a burden to others?

I don’t… I don’t think so, not exactly. I mean, I worry I’m a lot sometimes, or that people are tired of dealing with me, but I wouldn’t say I feel like a burden all the time.

Maybe I’m not explaining that very well. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
